"The idea that non consensus investing is where the alpha is, is actually quite dangerous in the early stage.

Follow on capital tends to be more and more consensus aligned."

"There's something tied to the ego and the identity of investors that they have to believe that they can truffle hunt and find the non-consensus thing. 

But the reality is, if you look at our portfolio, the ones that returned money were actually very, very competitive in general."

The Morning Minute (11.4)

⏰Top News:
-Crypto majors green after Dems sweep midterms; BTC at $78.2k
-Crypto’s $64M campaign against Sherrod Brown fails, several pro-crypto candidates lose
-Binance traced its $6.3B hack to a fake job interview & bad software download
-CFTC clears U.S. equity perps for trading; Citadel & others sue to stop it
-Circle reports earnings, revenue up 17% yoy (CRCL -3% premarket)

🌎 Macro Crypto and Markets
-Crypto majors are green post-Midterms with ZEC leading; BTC +1% at $78.2k; ETH +2% at $2,320; SOL even at $93; HYPE even at $84.5; ZEC +7% at $1,285
-LIT (+8%), VVV (+7%), RAY (+7%) and ENA (+5%) led top alt movers
-Oil -3% at $95; Gold +3% at $4,054
-Stock futures are green after the Democrat sweep; DOW +1.6%, Nasdaq +0.5%

-Crypto’s $64 million campaign against Sherrod Brown failed as he returns to the Senate, where he could land a committee leadership role with jurisdiction over the industry, capping a bruising night for crypto’s political operation; pro-crypto House Republicans Bryan Steil, Zach Nunn and Ann Wagner lost their seats, while Pete Ricketts held Nebraska and Andy Barr won Kentucky’s open Senate seat to replace Mitch McConnell

-Circle reported third-quarter revenue and reserve income of $865 million, up 17% year over year, with average USDC circulation reaching $73.3 billion

-Documentation platform GitBook disclosed a breach of its infrastructure credentials

-Justin Sun asked a federal court to sanction World Liberty Financial

-Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company holds “give or take 150,000 bitcoin”

David Pawlan, creator of Assistant Benchmark, has tracked 147 AI assistants so far, and in his group chats of AI power users, the number one fear is trust. It comes up in 22% of roughly 3,600 messages.

Top-quartile venture beat top-quartile buyout through the internet buildout and again through mobile and cloud, and a16z's Jen Kha argues we're at the start of the next wave.

Tech buyouts have long been the "safe" bet in private markets. Now the stress is showing:

- In the first half of 2026, venture funds marked their tech holdings up 16%, while buyout funds marked theirs down 4%

- 70% of the debt foreclosed in 2025 and 2026 came from deals done in 2021 or 2022

- A typical buyout now needs 10 to 12% EBITDA growth a year to make 2.5x in five years, up from about 5% in 2015

- Top 5% venture funds from 2007-16 returned 5.3x their capital in cash, versus 3.5x for top 5% buyout funds

"Tech buyout is a late-cycle asset class. It's most effective once a technology wave has settled and when business models are predictable enough to borrow against. When a new technology wave drops, all bets are off. By contrast, that's when venture shines."

Full piece from a16z's Jen Kha: https://t.co/FQ7O8OwBe3

Cyberoffense/defense is probably going to eat up a TON of compute and end up a continuous compute-intensive arms race. 

Even $AMZN CEO thinks cybersecurity would take up 20% of tokens consumed for the next year.

US spent $11T+ cumulatively (inflation adjusted) on Nuclear weapons and we're like ~$1.8T into the the "cyber-nuclear weapon" equivalent of that

And this is not even including the endless other economic implications from AI in other fields from advancing cancer discovery to workforce automation with physical AI. 

It's hard to measure AI sustainability if $50K in compute spend from a foreign actor can take down $10B of your own infrastructure. 

AI has become a bipartisan national security issue, and even Democrats would not want China overtake the US in this field.

tweets.text:
For companies like $SIVE / $AAOI, the demand imbalance for lasers are so severe

That even a 20-30% overall demand reduction from a hypothetical DC slowdown would likely not eliminate the shortage. 

We're seeing this before the next architectural shifts, where $NVDA Jensen Huang expects 15x optical volume for CPO scale-up. 

And as more hyperscalers commit to NPO as seen with $LITE new $5B UHP laser contracts. 

I'd argue this is more nuanced since I can't say the same for finished 800G/1.6T pluggables or lower end 70mW-100mW laser ranges that are currently bottlenecks. 

But this argument is more toward higher spec lasers. 

$AAOI is vertically integrated and has 300-400 mW capabilities, so they have the capability to shift attention to merchant lasers over supplying end-to-end optical transceivers. 

$SIVE is more pure play on this laser bottleneck, but they have the capabilities for 200mW + higher margin multiwavelength NPO/CPO lasers. 

I'd argue this is specifically the case for bottlenecks where demand imbalances are so deep (creating higher long term visibility, such as HBM). 

Whether it's large body substrates from $ATS that's bottlenecking Marvell + $AMD or lasers from $LITE that are sold out into 2029. 

or liquid transformers that have 4-5 year lead times. 

They they would still sell out of capacity even if overall demand decreased. 

If markets de-risked, it would make sense to hit optical module manufacturing players, maybe server rack assembly, to companies that still require heavy financing like Neoclouds.

And obviously haircut growth valuations (but not to the point where demand collapses to 0).

Yet we're seeing everything in AI trade is getting lumped up together as something that requires heavy financing + not profitable.

Little rant, but to show you how rampant deleveraging has become:

- $CIFR is worth 44% LESS than when they announced their initial $GOOGL / $AMZN colo deals. 

- $AAOI is now ~ the same price BEFORE they secured major hyperscaler orders, raised $1.6B for capacity expansion and gave their suprising initial -> $378M+ projection ->  ~$471M revenue forecast.

- $ESMT ($2B MC) is the perfect example representing the memory sector.

B-BUT AI NAMES ARE NOT PROFITABLE??? Q3 Earnings: $526.2M gross profit, $330M net income.

To give you a comparison of what that looks like, the net income of $CRWD ($251B MC) was literally $5.3M. 

$NOW ($113B MC) was $277M.
$TSLA ($1.5T) was $787M.

Different industries/durability, but if we care about what's actually hitting the balance sheet: 

ESMT is sitting on ~$937M in net assets ($740M net cash, $278M inventory, etc), so EV goes down to $1.2B ish.

Annualized P/E: 1.6x...

People keep saying "Peak Earnings", "Cyclical", "no moat" but who in the world would want to build an old ass DDR2 line + fab and qualify it?

From ESMT commentary, we'll likely see ASP hikes Q4 to make up for potential consumer demand dropping. 

And further supply tightening with Samsung/Micron discontinuing DDR2/DDR3 lines.

Winbond was leaving DDR2 lines to pursue higher end memory. People keep saying China, but even Gigadevice was leaving DDR3 to pursue higher end memory. "DDR3's share of our DRAM revenue will continue to decline until we eventually stop selling DDR3 products."Nanya discontinued DDR2 lines few days ago. 

This is while majority of ESMT revenue comes from DDR2/DDR3. In ~3 quarters of constant earnings, ESMT would have more assets than their entire MC.

Who is going to stop buying $40 DLink cameras if their $3 memory cost goes to $3.5?

$MU / Samsung / $SKHY / $SNDK share similar parallels where durability is contractually enforced via take/pay LTAs with price floors.

But markets are pretending that it just won't happen, despite Samsung already being the most profitable company in the world. 

Markets should care about how much FCF is actually hitting the balance sheets, but are just indiscriminately selling off everything now.

But continue rotating capital into 47x P/E companies like Walmart or 180x forward P/E names like $CRWD.

☢️ #Nuclear power is planning decades ahead. The #uranium mine pipeline needs to catch up. $M.CN $MYRUF is part of the answer.

The risk of a widening uranium supply deficit has several drivers:

▪️ LIFE EXTENSIONS
Keeping reactors operating for 60–80 years preserves decades of fuel demand that would otherwise disappear with retirement.

▪️ NEW NUCLEAR
Around 80 reactors are under construction worldwide. The World Nuclear Association’s reference scenario projects annual uranium requirements rising from roughly 69,000 tonnes in 2025 to more than 150,000 tonnes by 2040.

▪️ YEARS OF UNDERINVESTMENT
Weak uranium prices discouraged exploration and mine development for years. Spending is recovering, but rebuilding the project pipeline takes time.

▪️ TOO FEW NEW MINES ADVANCING FAST ENOUGH
Recent production growth has relied heavily on restarts and expansions. Uranium mine development typically takes 15–20 years.

▪️ EXISTING MINES DEPLETING
Future projects must replace declining production as well as supply additional reactors. Inventories and other secondary supplies have helped to help bridge the gap, but not for much longer.

Now add Kazakhstan’s latest move.
On November 3, Kazatomprom’s CEO briefed President Tokayev on work to establish a national strategic uranium reserve.

The broader proposal envisages reserving at least 150,000 tonnes of uranium by 2050 through a combination of deposits kept underground, physical uranium stocks and finished nuclear fuel. Implementation details remain under development.
To me, that reinforces how seriously at least some governments are taking long-term fuel security.

Against this backdrop, no wonder TradeTech’s long-term uranium price indicator reached $99/lb on October 31—an all-time high for its series, which began in 1996.
This is why I see strategic relevance in Myriad Uranium’s three wholly owned projects:

🇺🇸 COPPER MOUNTAIN, WYOMING
A historically explored uranium district with approximately 2,000 historical boreholes. Myriad’s current drilling is building modern data to support a future maiden resource estimate. That substantial historical foundation gives the company a focused starting point for exploration.

🇺🇸 ARIZONA BRECCIA PIPES
A portfolio of 24 prospects, including Wate, offers multiple targets in an established uranium-producing district. Historical work supports the exploration case, although historical estimates still require verification.

🇦🇷 LOS ALTARES, ARGENTINA
Acquired on November 2, this approximately 55,000-hectare project gives Myriad exposure to the Cerro Solo uranium district. It includes granted concessions and approved environmental assessments on certain properties, with potential for in-situ recovery still requiring technical testing.

Myriad also retains a 10% free-carried interest in Red Basin.

Three wholly owned projects. Different geological opportunities. Two countries.

Tomorrow’s uranium supply requires exploration investment today.

Disclosure: Paid partnership with Myriad Uranium. Please do your own research.

🇺🇸 A 92% headline premium puts U.S. #uranium M&A in focus.

Eagle #Nuclear Energy $NUCL has signed a binding LOI to acquire Noble Plains Uranium $NOBL in an all-share transaction.

The proposed terms:

▪️ 0.0167 Eagle shares per Noble Plains share
▪️ C$0.125 deemed value per share
▪️ ~92% premium to Noble Plains’ October 29 close

The strategic angle? Wyoming ISR potential alongside Eagle’s conventional uranium project in Oregon.
Duck Creek hosts 5.32M lbs indicated + 1.04M lbs inferred U₃O₈, reported on a 100% basis. Noble Plains holds an option to acquire 80%.
And that resource covers just 2.5 miles of a 5.25-mile trend, entirely within the shallower of two prospective formations. Room to explore.

My take: combining established resources, exploration upside and different development routes makes this worth watching.

Still an LOI: a definitive agreement and approvals remain outstanding. The all-share consideration also means the value moves with $NUCL.

The real test now: turning a larger U.S. uranium portfolio into future supply.

tweets.full_text:
In May 1996, under the Gateway Arch in St. Louis, I used that inspiration to challenge private teams to fly a reusable spaceship to space twice within two weeks.

Behind me stood 20 astronauts, including Buzz Aldrin, plus Lindbergh’s grandson, Erik, and NASA Administrator Dan Goldin.

They thought I was being reckless, and in retrospect, I was.
The idea for creating this came from Lindbergh. In 1927, a $25,000 prize for the first nonstop flight from New York to Paris drove nine teams to spend $400,000. Only the winner got paid.

How I launched the first XPRIZE

Two board members resigned when I told them how much money I needed to launch the first XPRIZE. We had raised $500,000, and I wanted to spend it all announcing a $10 million competition. The truth was, I didn’t have the $10 million.

I call this launching “above the line of super-credibility.” When an idea is born above that line, people’s focus shifts from probabilities to implications. They stop asking whether it can happen and start asking HOW to be part of it.

Then I learned Anousheh Ansari wanted to fly on a suborbital flight. I pitched her, and she eventually said yes (after tracking her down while she was vacationing in Hawaii).

Here’s the truth, however: credibility didn’t make funding appear overnight. For five years, I pitched 150 people and heard the same questions every time: “Why isn’t NASA doing this? Can anyone really pull it off? Isn’t someone going to die trying?”

The reason I’m telling you all of this is that many of us have felt self-doubt or uncertainty about how to proceed when things get tough. Two board members calling you reckless is enough to make anyone doubt themselves. For five years, every “no” was a chance to quit.

Eventually, 26 teams invested more than $100 million chasing our $10 million prize. In 2004, SpaceShipOne won.

By then, all three questions had answers. NASA didn’t need to do it. A private team pulled it off. And no one was hurt.

The doubt will not go away on its own. You just need to stop letting it take control of your life.

So what’s the idea you’ve been waiting on, and what would it take to start before you feel ready?

Credibility got people to listen. Refusing to quit got it funded. Uncertain times don’t mean you should wait.

A lot of people are heading into hard years right now, unsure whether to bet on themselves. I understand that. I was there for five years with a $10 million promise and no $10 million.

tweets.text:
Assessing Data Center Risk After a Texas Surprise
While the markets were pricing in a Democratic takeover of both the House and the Senate to some extent, we believe the magnitude of the win was unexpected. Most notably, a new Democratic Governor in Texas was not our base case, we think this introduces new questions and greater uncertainty for many PSPs operating in that region. We believe states with available power and comparatively lower near-term political risk, such as North Dakota, Louisiana and Kentucky, could stand to benefit from a potential moratorium on Texas data centers.

All Eyes on Texas: Texas holds ~30% of data center capacity currently under construction nationally, and Governor-elect Hinojosa has floated a broad moratorium on new sites until new legislation can be put in place. With the scope, mechanism and timeline all undefined, we expect greater uncertainty to continue to drive a risk-off reaction to many Texas based operators. Governor Abbott currently has two months left in office and retains the ability to push project approvals through before handoff, a dynamic that could favor operators who are already energized or sit at the front of ERCOT's interconnection queue.

Key Questions the market is Asking:
Scope and mechanism of a moratorium: Would it cover only new applications or also projects under      construction or with an interconnect agreement in hand?
PUCT Control: With two seats expiring in September 2027, could Hinojosa's appointments change the trajectory of ERCOT into 2028?
Fate of the ERCOT Process: Will ERCOT's interconnection process continue as planned?
Energization dates: Is a reasonable base case that the mega projects with energization dates in proceed as planned?
Grandfathering of executed agreements: For sites planned in 2H27 and beyond, is a signed PPA or interconnection agreement protected from retroactive review or do those publicly committed project timelines still hold if tenants are already secured (such as HUT's Beacon Point Phase 2 project with a signed tenant)?
Sales-tax repeal bill: With the bill already advancing in the Senate under GOP control, will the trajectory change under a Democratic governor?

The bull case for oil from the Saudi Aramco conference call yesterday:

“Since disruptions began, the global market has lost over 3 billion barrels of liquid supply. Alternative flows including export via our East-West pipeline and strategic petroleum reserve releases have narrowed the cumulative deficit to around 2 billion barrels. The remaining gap was balanced by demand management and substantial withdrawals from commercial inventories. While these actions have bought time, they are not a permanent solution.”

“The resulting market tightness is increasingly evident in physical prices. Buyers competing for immediately available barrels have driven physical prices above futures, and strong demand with constrained supplies has pushed refining margins to record levels.”

“Looking ahead, the market faces additional pressure from both seasonal and structural demand. Global product stocks are now alarmingly low, particularly for diesel, and with diesel demand expected to increase further in Q4, the market faces further pressure heading into winter. In 2027, global liquids demand is projected to expand by around 2.4 million barrels per day as demand management measures ease.”

“Beyond meeting additional demand, the market also faces the challenge of replenishing depleted inventories. More oil will be needed to rebuild inventories and fill additional storage capacity, a process which could take up to two years.”

tweets.text:
I don't know what the future will bring. A world where the situation with Iran does not improve, already historically low crude inventories evaporate, refined products blow up and the ensuing unrelenting inflation pushes the Fed and other central banks from hawkish to very hawkish, ending this cycle, is definitely feasible. 

However, there's a ton of AI doom in the air, last week's deleveraging and the recent crash across momentum assets are historical outliers, post-midterm price action was very positive (it reminded me of a miniature version of Trump's 2016 victory), high-risk earnings are mostly behind us, the front end of the Treasury curve already has two more hikes priced in by March, Brent is at 102, and the blue sweep should reduce war-risk premia (lower odds of Trump going wild in the Middle East - if he did, the Senate could revolt against him, and the odds of a House impeachment turning into a Trump removal would no longer be zero, though still small).

Therefore, I think it is time to go risk-on and bet on historical post-midterm seasonality with a 3 month horizon. I like Mag 7 (ex TSLA, too soon to fade the midterms), solar energy, and I continue to like long bonds as a growth-scare hedge. Among data centers, I like those with no Texas exposure (TeraWulf), as Texas unexpectedly electing a Democrat Governor reshapes the landscape. 

Good luck trading

I don't think engineers will start from a blank file anymore. They will point a swarm of agents at a problem like building a website and watch them work.

Agents  open the best apps in a real browser. They inspect the DOM, dump every network request, and map the backend. They use computer use to click through every flow like a real user. Then they rebuild it, piece by piece, while you watch the code appear.

And then agents plug in customer telemetry. The agents read customer feedback in the inbox. They ship dozens of features, they run A/B tests live, see what sticks, and kill the rest. Unit tests, performance, and load times get checked on every change.

The loop never stops. I made this video to show what I have in mind. The hard part won't be writing the code anymore. It will be knowing what's worth building.

tweets.text: mSAP is modified semi-additive. Start from a few microns of foil, pattern plate the traces up through dry film, then flash etch the seed. Etching thick foil gets you 50 um plus trapezoidal lines. mSAP gets 25 to 30 um lines with a near-rectangular cross section, which keeps impedance in tolerance. Phones went there with the iPhone X in 2017. A 1.6T module runs eight 200G PAM4 lanes at about 106 GBaud, Nyquist near 53 GHz, on a 1.0 mm OSFP board. You can't hold a 3 mil differential stripline at +/-5% with etched traces, so mSAP it is. (2/4)

thread_tweets.text: The specs on dimensions are rigrous. Board thickness +/-75 um on a 1.0 mm board. Outline, gold finger and hole positions at +/-50 um, non-plated drills at +/-12.5 um. Strip warpage under 10 um, solder mask flatness under 5 um. All of it has to hold at once, and a line tuned for phone boards doesn't hold it on day one. The items that bite are the high-speed and via work. Holding +/-5% impedance on a 3 mil stripline, about 75 um wide, ringless vias on the high-speed nets with no annular ring, and keeping the via fill dimple under 5 um are the rows graded high risk. Filled through holes with 100 um drills in thin cores sit a notch easier. (3/4)
